acceptance_criteria: enrichGO (BP and MF) run on up- and down-regulated DE gene lists (FDR<0.05, |LFC|>=1) with universe = all tested genes and BH adjustment; results tables with q-values written to CSV

If org.Dr.eg.db cannot map the dataset's identifiers, the mapping-failure rate is reported and the step falls back to what the installed resources support rather than failing silently

steps.name: Orthology-projected pathway enrichment (human WikiPathways/KEGG)
caveats: Human pathway hits are cross-species inferences, not zebrafish pathway measurements — label them as orthology-projected in all outputs
The MSigDB KEGG collection is the MEDICUS subset; set names/membership differ from legacy KEGG and must not be compared across releases
steps.question: Which named canonical pathways (WikiPathways, KEGG MEDICUS) do the treated-vs-control DE genes point to, via human orthologs of the zebrafish genes?
steps.description: Use the installed babelgene ortholog tables (Ensembl Compara, includes Danio rerio) to project zebrafish DE genes and the full ranked list onto human gene symbols, then run ORA and preranked GSEA against the WikiPathways human 2026-07-10 GMT and the MSigDB C2:CP KEGG MEDICUS human GMT that are staged as reference data. This is the only route to named pathways here: no zebrafish pathway GMT exists in the reference store.
acceptance_criteria: Ortholog mapping coverage reported (n and % of DE genes and of the ranked list mapped to a unique human symbol); one-to-many orthologs resolved by a stated rule (e.g. best-supported or one-to-one only)
ORA on mapped up/down DE lists against the human WikiPathways 2026-07-10 GMT and the MSigDB C2:CP KEGG MEDICUS GMT, universe = mapped tested genes, BH-adjusted; results to CSV
Preranked GSEA on the mapped full ranking against both GMT collections with a fixed seed; top enriched pathways plotted

If babelgene carries no Danio rerio orthologs or mapping coverage is too low (<50% of DE genes), the step reports the coverage, states that pathway-level interpretation is restricted to the GO results, and still delivers the GO step's output unchanged
